summary: A lightstation on a puffin rock at the western end of the Mingan Archipelago, lit in 1888 and kept by a French count, a diarist-fisherman and a keeper whose wife wrote a book.

notes_for_editor: Keepers' dates rest on Lighthouse Friends' list, Vigneau's own journal and the Quebec heritage register; the Department of Marine salary tables are OCR column dumps and were used only where the keeper's name sat next to the station (1915 'H. Vignaux'; 1908 'Perroquet Placide Vigneau' not cited). Accounts differ on the Forgues widow's delivery (Lighthouse Friends: no doctor; Vigneau: she bore a girl after 10 May; nosorigines.qc.ca says the drowning came three days before the birth, not read). Diaphone date 1918 vs report printed 1920. Hector Vigneault: relationship to Placide not sourced here (Wikipedia says son, not cited). Kavanagh's ice crossing is dated December 1954 by Québec maritime; Lighthouse Friends gives no date. Today access: LF says tower closed; the park page says Parks Canada manages the island (not cited here as owner). No Wikipedia cited. Mary Collin-Kavanagh named only as the source names her, as author. Not found: lens details beyond the 1888 report; 1981 automation not confirmed by a read source (record's brief only). Verified 2026-10-27: Lighthouse Friends says Forgues crossed for a doctor, Vigneau says chimneys (stated in story). Vigneau's 'près de vingt ans' of petitions vs the 1877 first request (11 years) noted in story. 'mulerons' rendered as haystacks.
